questions.question: Which countries make up the United Kingdom (UK)?
options: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland
England, Wales and the Republic of Ireland
questions.explanation: The UK consists of four countries: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland. Great Britain is only the island with England, Scotland and Wales.

questions.question: What is "Great Britain"?
options: The island that includes England, Scotland and Wales
questions.explanation: Great Britain is the island containing England, Scotland and Wales. The UK also includes Northern Ireland.

questions.question: What is the capital of Scotland?
questions.explanation: Edinburgh is the capital of Scotland. Cardiff is the capital of Wales and Belfast of Northern Ireland.

questions.question: Why is it wrong to call the whole UK "England"?
options: Because Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are separate countries within the UK
Because England is not part of the UK
Because "England" is the name of the capital
questions.explanation: England is only one of the four countries in the UK. Scots, Welsh and Northern Irish people do not appreciate being called English.

questions.question: What is the capital of Wales?
questions.explanation: Cardiff is the capital of Wales. London is the capital of England (and the UK), and Dublin is the capital of the Republic of Ireland.
